Election Commission Faces Scrutiny Over Internal Dissent and SIR Decisions

A report indicates that two out of three Election Commissioners raised objections 14 times in 10 months concerning changes to Form 6 and SIR voter deletion appeals. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has responded by stating that decisions are unanimous and that internal suggestions from commissioners are a standard administrative process aimed at improving electoral procedures. The ECI clarified that field officials retain statutory powers and that the ECINet system is decentralized, preventing unauthorized actions. Following the report of a divide within the commission, opposition parties have called for a Supreme Court-monitored probe and for the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) to step down, while distancing the CEC from the commission's overall functioning. Some coverage also revisits past controversies and debates surrounding the composition of the Election Commission.
